newsitem.title: UK: UK's ITC watchdog calls for single TV regulator.
newsitem.headline: UK's ITC watchdog calls for single TV regulator.

text.p: The Independent Television Commission on Tuesday called for a single broadcasting regulator, charging that the current system of more than four watchdogs was complicated and potentially costly and confusing.

In a memorandum to the Select Committee on National Heritage, the Commission said it recognised that any rationalisation of the regulatory structure would need considerable debate and much detailed work.
But it stated: "A single regulator -- with the right portfolio of powers and sanctions -- would be best placed to deliver effective and cost-effective regulation."

The BBC, in particular, was operating in a changing environment and its self-regulatory system would come under increasing strain as it became more involved in commercial ventures as part of its operations, the ITC argued.
Regulatory watchdogs responsible for some aspects of broadcasting regulation include the ITC, the BBC, the soon-to-be-merged Broadcasting Standards Council and the Broadcasting Complaints Commission.
